items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: Benny Goodman, he was up every morning.

ctx.x: So I had to go where the old ones went. I followed them. Come on, Scottie, you going? I say, where are you going? Well, never mind, come on, you're with me. Go this place and that place. So after we got out, anytime it'd be daylight, we'd get out of those places. And fellows have money, never nobody hold you up or nothing like that. The white fellows used to come uptown, they'd get through and they'd come by the Nest and like that. They'd cross the street, 33rd Street,

there was Mexico's, Pod's and Jerry's, private houses in the basement there, they used to have a piano. Now, you could go in there and buy a drink, because it didn't cost nothing then, and sit down, and you could play if you wanted. Piano players would come in -- those white fellows -- Benny Goodman, he was up every morning. So was Harry James, so was the fellow -- I could go on, name after name. They used to come up and jam, and jamming there, they would listen, stuff like that.

Even one time had Louis up there. He was jamming Saturday nights at Lafayette Hall. That was a big hall on the 31st Street side. And all of them used to come up, because naturally, they have a pencil, they'd take down a riff if they liked something. A little later came a new record and you'd hear that same riff.
